capstone.title: Assess a RAG Support Agent End to End
capstone.desc: Threat model a RAG assistant, probe injection and leakage, inspect the pipeline and agent permissions, map findings to OWASP LLM, and brief a fix plan.

cert_note: Supports OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI RMF knowledge; useful context for CompTIA SecAI+ and ISO 42001 study. Guide only.

can_do: Distinguish supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning
Trace data through an ML pipeline from ingestion to deployment
Interpret precision, recall and confusion matrices for a model

lessons.title: Machine learning concepts and paradigms
lessons.goal: Explain supervised, unsupervised, self-supervised and reinforcement learning with security-relevant examples.

lessons.title: Training versus inference
lessons.goal: Describe training and inference and where each phase exposes data, weights and compute to attack.

lessons.title: Neural networks: layers, weights, gradients
lessons.goal: Explain neurons, activations, loss functions and backpropagation at a conceptual level.

lessons.title: Data pipelines and feature engineering
lessons.goal: Map ingestion, labeling, cleaning, splitting and feature stores, and name the trust boundaries in each stage.

lessons.title: Evaluating models: metrics and overfitting
lessons.goal: Compute accuracy, precision, recall and F1 from a confusion matrix and spot overfitting from train/test gaps.

lessons.title: Common model types and where they are used
lessons.goal: Match classifiers, regressors, CNNs, RNNs, tree ensembles, GANs and diffusion models to security use cases.

labs.title: Read a confusion matrix
labs.task: Given a malware classifier's results, compute precision, recall and F1 and decide if it is fit for blocking.

labs.title: Draw the ML pipeline trust boundaries
labs.task: Place data source, labeling, training, registry and serving nodes and mark where untrusted input enters.

labs.title: Spot overfitting in training logs
labs.task: Read epoch logs of train versus validation loss and identify the epoch where the model begins to overfit.

labs.title: Run a toy classifier
labs.task: Use scikit-learn commands to train, split and score a spam classifier, then compare two feature sets.

checkpoint.focus: Training vs inference, pipeline stages, confusion-matrix metrics, overfitting and model type selection

can_do: Explain tokenization, embeddings and attention in plain terms
Describe how RAG, fine-tuning and agents extend a base model
Predict how context window limits and prompt structure affect output

lessons.title: Tokens and tokenization
lessons.goal: Explain how BPE tokenizers split text, why token counts drive cost and limits, and cause quirks.

lessons.title: Embeddings and vector similarity
lessons.goal: Explain embeddings, cosine similarity and vector databases, and why nearest-neighbor search powers retrieval.

lessons.title: Transformers and attention, intuitively
lessons.goal: Describe self-attention, next-token prediction and sampling parameters (temperature, top-p) without the math.

lessons.title: Context windows and prompt structure
lessons.goal: Explain system, user and assistant roles, context limits, and how instruction priority is (not) enforced.

lessons.title: RAG and fine-tuning
lessons.goal: Compare retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning and LoRA, and list the data-exposure risks of each.

lessons.title: Agents, tools and function calling
lessons.goal: Describe the agent loop, function-calling schemas and MCP, and where untrusted text enters the loop.

labs.title: Count tokens and estimate cost
labs.task: Run a tokenizer on sample prompts, compare token counts across strings and compute a request cost.

labs.title: Tune sampling parameters
labs.task: Adjust temperature and top-p on a sandbox model and record how determinism and risk of odd output change.

labs.title: Trace a RAG request
labs.task: Order the query, embedding, vector search, prompt assembly and generation steps and tag untrusted data paths.

labs.title: Review an agent tool schema
labs.task: Read a function-calling JSON schema and identify which parameters accept free text from the model.

checkpoint.focus: Tokens, embeddings, attention intuition, context limits, RAG versus fine-tuning, agent loop

can_do: Enumerate the attack surface of an AI system end to end
Build a threat model for an ML-backed application
Map observed attacks to MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI 100-2 categories

lessons.title: The AI attack surface
lessons.goal: List attack points across data, training, model artifacts, serving APIs, plugins and users.

lessons.title: Threat modeling AI systems
lessons.goal: Apply STRIDE and data flow diagrams to an ML app, adding model and data-specific threats.

lessons.title: MITRE ATLAS tactics and techniques
lessons.goal: Navigate ATLAS tactics from reconnaissance to impact and map case studies to technique IDs such as AML.T0051.

lessons.title: NIST adversarial ML taxonomy
lessons.goal: Use NIST AI 100-2 to classify evasion, poisoning, privacy and abuse attacks by attacker goal and knowledge.

lessons.title: Attacker capabilities and risk rating
lessons.goal: Rate threats by access level (white, gray, black box), impact and likelihood, and choose mitigations.

labs.title: Threat model a chatbot
labs.task: Draw a data flow diagram for a support chatbot and annotate trust boundaries and AI-specific threats.

labs.title: Map an incident to ATLAS
labs.task: Read a short incident description and select the matching ATLAS tactics and technique IDs in order.

labs.title: Classify attacks by NIST taxonomy
labs.task: Sort ten attack summaries into evasion, poisoning, privacy or abuse and name attacker knowledge level.

labs.title: Triage AI findings by risk
labs.task: Review alerts from an inference gateway and rank them by likelihood and impact using the threat model.

checkpoint.focus: AI attack surface, STRIDE for ML, ATLAS technique mapping, NIST AI 100-2 classes

can_do: Recognize direct and indirect prompt injection payloads
Apply layered guardrails and test them with an evaluation set
Measure defense effectiveness with attack success rate

lessons.title: Direct prompt injection
lessons.goal: Explain how user text overrides instructions and craft benign test payloads for instruction hijacking.

lessons.title: Indirect prompt injection
lessons.goal: Describe how poisoned web pages, emails and documents inject instructions through retrieved content.

lessons.title: Jailbreak patterns
lessons.goal: Recognize role-play, encoding, multi-turn escalation and many-shot jailbreaks and why they work.

lessons.title: Input and output guardrails
lessons.goal: Configure classifiers, allow-lists, delimiters and output filters, and state their known bypass limits.

lessons.title: Architectural defenses
lessons.goal: Apply privilege separation, dual-LLM patterns, structured outputs and context isolation to limit impact.

lessons.title: Evaluating defenses
lessons.goal: Build a test set, compute attack success rate and false positive rate, and compare guardrail configurations.

lessons.title: Tooling: Garak, PyRIT and Promptfoo
lessons.goal: Run automated probes and read their reports to find regressions after prompt or model changes.

labs.title: Classify injection attempts
labs.task: Label fifteen prompts as benign, direct injection, indirect injection or jailbreak and justify each.

labs.title: Hijack a sandbox assistant
labs.task: Use a harmless canary instruction to override a sandbox system prompt, then document the transcript.

labs.title: Find the poisoned document
labs.task: Browse a RAG corpus of files and locate the document carrying a hidden instruction payload.

labs.title: Harden a system prompt and filter
labs.task: Edit delimiters and output filter rules, then rerun the test set to lower attack success rate.

labs.title: Run a Garak probe
labs.task: Run a garak probe against a mock endpoint and interpret the pass/fail summary per probe.

checkpoint.focus: Direct vs indirect injection, jailbreak families, layered defenses, ASR and false positive metrics

can_do: Name and explain each OWASP LLM Top 10 risk
Identify vulnerable patterns in LLM application code and config
Recommend a control for each risk category

lessons.title: OWASP LLM Top 10 overview
lessons.goal: Walk through the current list, its risk ranking logic and how it relates to ATLAS and NIST AI RMF.

lessons.title: LLM01 Prompt injection and LLM05 output handling
lessons.goal: Explain how unvalidated model output reaches shells, SQL, HTML and templates, causing XSS or RCE.

lessons.title: Sensitive information disclosure
lessons.goal: Describe leakage of secrets, PII and system prompts through training data, context and logs, and mitigations.

lessons.title: Supply chain risks
lessons.goal: Identify risks in third-party models, datasets and plugins, and verify with hashes and SBOM/AIBOM.

lessons.title: Data and model poisoning
lessons.goal: Explain how tampered training or fine-tuning data creates integrity failures and how to detect it.

lessons.title: Excessive agency
lessons.goal: Recognize excessive functionality, permissions and autonomy in agents and apply least privilege and approval.

lessons.title: System prompt leakage and vector weaknesses
lessons.goal: Assess exposed system prompts and RAG access-control gaps such as cross-tenant retrieval.

lessons.title: Misinformation and unbounded consumption
lessons.goal: Handle hallucinated output, overreliance and denial-of-wallet with grounding, rate limits and quotas.

labs.title: Exploit an output handling flaw
labs.task: In a sandbox chat app, intercept a response containing script markup and show it executing in the page.

labs.title: Fix unsafe output code
labs.task: Patch an app that passes model output to eval or a SQL string with encoding and parameterized queries.

labs.title: Find leaked secrets in logs
labs.task: Search LLM request logs for API keys, PII and system prompt text and list the exposure paths.

labs.title: Audit agent permissions
labs.task: Reduce a tool manifest from admin scope to least privilege and add approval for destructive actions.

labs.title: Check cross-tenant retrieval
labs.task: Query a sandbox vector store with two tenant tokens and prove which one can read the other's documents.

labs.title: Match risks to controls
labs.task: Match eight application scenarios to the correct OWASP LLM risk and its primary mitigation.

checkpoint.focus: OWASP LLM Top 10 risks, vulnerable patterns, excessive agency, disclosure, supply chain controls

can_do: Describe how poisoning, backdoor and evasion attacks work
Explain extraction and privacy attacks and their prerequisites
Select defenses suited to each attack class

lessons.title: Data poisoning
lessons.goal: Explain label flipping and clean-label poisoning, how little data is needed and how to sanitize datasets.

lessons.title: Backdoors and trojaned models
lessons.goal: Describe trigger-based backdoors, BadNets and sleeper behavior, and detection with Neural Cleanse style tests.

lessons.title: Adversarial examples and evasion
lessons.goal: Explain FGSM and PGD perturbations, transferability and robustness measures like adversarial training.

lessons.title: Model extraction and stealing
lessons.goal: Describe query-based cloning, API rate limits, output perturbation and watermarking as countermeasures.

lessons.title: Membership inference
lessons.goal: Explain how confidence gaps reveal training membership and how regularization and DP reduce it.

lessons.title: Model inversion and training data extraction
lessons.goal: Describe reconstruction of training samples and LLM memorization extraction attacks.

lessons.title: Defense selection and trade-offs
lessons.goal: Compare robustness, privacy and accuracy trade-offs and pick controls per threat and attacker access.

labs.title: Spot poisoned training samples
labs.task: Inspect a labeled image dataset and flag samples with flipped labels and a repeated trigger patch.

labs.title: Run FGSM in a sandbox
labs.task: Execute a provided FGSM script on a toy classifier and report the epsilon at which prediction flips.

labs.title: Detect extraction in API logs
labs.task: Query inference logs for high-volume systematic queries from one key and write a detection rule.

labs.title: Score membership inference risk
labs.task: Complete a short script comparing confidence on train versus test samples and compute the attack AUC.

labs.title: Choose defenses per attack
labs.task: Pick rate limiting, DP, adversarial training or data vetting for five described attacks and justify.

checkpoint.focus: Poisoning, backdoors, adversarial examples, extraction, membership inference and matching defenses

can_do: Verify provenance and integrity of datasets and models
Identify unsafe serialization and scan model files
Design access control and drift monitoring for ML pipelines

lessons.title: Data provenance and lineage
lessons.goal: Track dataset origin, versions and transformations with DVC or hashes and verify trust before training.

lessons.title: Model registries and access control
lessons.goal: Configure registry roles, stage promotion and separation of duties for training, approval and deployment.

lessons.title: Model signing and integrity
lessons.goal: Sign and verify model artifacts with Sigstore or cosign and hash-pin dependencies.

lessons.title: Unsafe serialization: pickle and friends
lessons.goal: Explain how pickle deserialization gives code execution and why safetensors and ONNX reduce the risk.

lessons.title: Scanning and securing ML supply chain
lessons.goal: Use tools such as picklescan and ModelScan, SBOM and AIBOM, and vet hub downloads.

lessons.title: Drift monitoring and pipeline observability
lessons.goal: Detect data and concept drift with PSI or KS tests and alert on pipeline tampering and anomalies.

labs.title: Inspect a pickle for payloads
labs.task: Disassemble a sandbox pickle file with pickletools and identify the malicious reduce call.

labs.title: Scan a model hub download
labs.task: Run a model scanner on three artifacts and decide which to quarantine based on the findings.

labs.title: Verify a signed model
labs.task: Run signature and hash verification commands and explain why one artifact fails verification.

labs.title: Tighten registry permissions
labs.task: Edit role bindings so training jobs cannot promote models to production without approval.

checkpoint.focus: Provenance, signing, pickle risks, scanning tools, registry access control, drift detection

can_do: Apply least privilege and sandboxing to AI agents
Assess MCP servers and connectors for risk
Design human-in-the-loop approval and secret handling

lessons.title: Agent architecture and risk model
lessons.goal: Describe planner, memory and tool components and the confused deputy problem in agent systems.

lessons.title: Least privilege and tool permissions
lessons.goal: Scope tool access with per-tool allow-lists, read-only defaults and short-lived scoped credentials.

lessons.title: Sandboxing agent execution
lessons.goal: Isolate code execution using containers, seccomp, network egress rules and filesystem limits.

lessons.title: Connectors and MCP security
lessons.goal: Review MCP servers for tool poisoning, over-broad scopes, rug pulls and unvetted third-party code.

lessons.title: Human in the loop
lessons.goal: Design approval gates by action risk, avoid approval fatigue and log decisions for audit.

lessons.title: Secrets and audit logging
lessons.goal: Keep secrets out of prompts and context, use vault references and trace tool calls for forensics.

labs.title: Review an MCP tool manifest
labs.task: Find poisoned tool descriptions and excess scopes in an MCP config and remove or restrict them.

labs.title: Trace an agent incident
labs.task: Follow an agent's tool call log to find the step where injected text triggered an unauthorized action.

labs.title: Sandbox an agent runtime
labs.task: Set container egress rules, read-only mounts and resource limits for an agent code tool.

labs.title: Design approval policy
labs.task: Classify twelve agent actions as auto-approve, require approval or deny and set the policy.

checkpoint.focus: Least privilege, sandboxing, MCP and connector risks, approval gates, secret handling

can_do: Scope an AI red team engagement with clear rules
Run structured and automated probes against a model application
Report findings with severity, evidence and remediation

lessons.title: Scoping and rules of engagement
lessons.goal: Define targets, harm categories, authorization, data handling and stop conditions for an AI red team.

lessons.title: Test planning and harm taxonomies
lessons.goal: Build a test plan mapped to OWASP LLM, ATLAS and harm categories such as bias, toxicity and misuse.

lessons.title: Manual adversarial testing
lessons.goal: Apply creative prompts, multi-turn strategies and tool abuse to find failures, and log reproducible steps.

lessons.title: Automated probing tools
lessons.goal: Use Garak, PyRIT and Promptfoo to generate attacks at scale and tune scoring.

lessons.title: Safety and robustness evaluations
lessons.goal: Run benchmark-style evaluations, measure refusal and over-refusal rates and interpret metrics.

lessons.title: Reporting and retesting
lessons.goal: Write findings with severity, reproduction, impact, remediation and verify fixes with regression tests.

labs.title: Write a rules of engagement
labs.task: Complete a scope template listing in-scope models, forbidden actions and escalation contacts.

labs.title: Probe a sandbox chatbot
labs.task: Execute a planned set of misuse and injection tests and record which succeeded.

labs.title: Run PyRIT-style automation
labs.task: Launch an automated attack run, then read the scored results and pick top findings to verify manually.

labs.title: Draft a finding
labs.task: Rate severity and write reproduction steps, impact and fix for a discovered data leak.

checkpoint.focus: Scoping, test plan design, automated probing, safety metrics and report quality

can_do: Identify privacy risks across the AI data lifecycle
Explain differential privacy and federated learning
Map AI data handling to GDPR and similar regulations

lessons.title: Training data privacy and PII leakage
lessons.goal: Describe memorization, PII in datasets and prompts, and controls such as redaction and data minimization.

lessons.title: Differential privacy and federated learning
lessons.goal: Explain epsilon, noise addition, DP-SGD and federated averaging with their limits and trade-offs.

lessons.title: Regulations: GDPR, CCPA and consent
lessons.goal: Apply lawful basis, purpose limitation, data subject rights and DPIAs to AI systems.

lessons.title: Privacy engineering for LLM apps
lessons.goal: Implement PII detection, retention limits, log scrubbing and vendor data processing terms.

labs.title: Redact PII before logging
labs.task: Write regex and NER-style rules that mask emails, phone numbers and IDs in prompts, then test on samples.

labs.title: Find PII in a dataset
labs.task: Browse training files, tag records containing personal data and decide remove, mask or retain.

labs.title: Run a mini DPIA
labs.task: Answer assessment questions for a customer-chat feature and choose controls for each identified privacy risk.

checkpoint.focus: Memorization, PII controls, differential privacy and federated learning basics, GDPR duties

can_do: Apply NIST AI RMF functions to an AI system
Classify a system under the EU AI Act risk tiers
Respond to and document an AI incident

lessons.title: NIST AI RMF: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage
lessons.goal: Apply the four functions and the trustworthiness characteristics to a use case.

lessons.title: ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system
lessons.goal: Describe the AIMS clauses, Annex A controls and how they fit with ISO 27001.

lessons.title: EU AI Act risk tiers and obligations
lessons.goal: Classify prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk and minimal-risk systems and list provider duties.

lessons.title: Model cards, documentation and responsible AI
lessons.goal: Write model cards and datasheets covering intended use, limits, bias results and monitoring.

lessons.title: AI incident handling
lessons.goal: Adapt incident response to model failures, harmful outputs and data leaks, with reporting and lessons learned.

labs.title: Classify under the EU AI Act
labs.task: Sort six described systems into EU AI Act risk tiers and list the obligations that apply.

labs.title: Complete a model card
labs.task: Fill in intended use, training data, evaluation results and limitations fields for a sample model.

labs.title: Map controls to NIST AI RMF
labs.task: Place risk controls under Govern, Map, Measure and Manage for a hiring-screen model.

labs.title: Triage an AI incident
labs.task: Work through a harmful-output report by choosing containment, evidence collection and notification steps.

checkpoint.focus: AI RMF functions, ISO 42001 structure, EU AI Act tiers, documentation and incident response

can_do: Use AI to speed up SOC triage and summaries safely
Evaluate AI detection and anomaly tools with real metrics
Spot and handle hallucinated security output

lessons.title: AI in the SOC: triage and summarization
lessons.goal: Apply LLMs to alert enrichment, case summaries and query drafting with human validation.

lessons.title: AI-assisted detection engineering
lessons.goal: Generate and validate Sigma or KQL rules with AI, testing against sample logs before deployment.

lessons.title: Phishing detection with ML
lessons.goal: Describe feature-based and language-model phishing classifiers and their evasion weaknesses.

lessons.title: Anomaly detection basics
lessons.goal: Explain baselines, isolation forests and UEBA scoring, and manage false positives.

lessons.title: Hallucination risks in security work
lessons.goal: Identify fabricated CVEs, commands and indicators and apply verification habits.

lessons.title: Judging AI security tools
lessons.goal: Evaluate vendor claims using precision, recall, data handling, explainability and pilot results.

labs.title: Triage alerts with AI summaries
labs.task: Review AI-generated summaries of five alerts, verify them against raw events and mark which are wrong.

labs.title: Validate an AI-written detection
labs.task: Test a generated Sigma rule against sample logs, fix a logic error and reduce false positives.

labs.title: Catch a hallucinated IOC
labs.task: Question an AI assistant's report and verify each CVE and hash, flagging the fabricated ones.

labs.title: Score a vendor tool
labs.task: Compare two AI detection products on supplied metrics and choose one with written justification.

checkpoint.focus: AI in SOC workflows, detection validation, anomaly basics, hallucination checks, tool evaluation

can_do: Recognize deepfake and voice-clone fraud techniques
Identify AI-written phishing and automated attack traits
Apply layered detection and organizational defenses

lessons.title: Deepfakes and synthetic media
lessons.goal: Explain how face and video synthesis works and list visual and metadata cues of manipulation.

lessons.title: Voice cloning and vishing
lessons.goal: Describe cloning from short samples, CEO-fraud scenarios and callback or code-word verification.

lessons.title: AI-written phishing and social engineering
lessons.goal: Compare LLM-generated lures with traditional ones and adjust email controls and training.

lessons.title: Automated attacks and AI-assisted malware
lessons.goal: Describe automated recon, exploit generation and polymorphism, and what defenders should expect.

lessons.title: Detection and organizational defenses
lessons.goal: Apply C2PA provenance, liveness checks, out-of-band verification and payment approval controls.

labs.title: Verify a suspicious voice request
labs.task: Handle a cloned-voice payment request by choosing verification steps and escalation.

labs.title: Analyze a phishing email set
labs.task: Inspect headers and body of eight emails and decide which look AI-generated and which authentication checks fail.

labs.title: Inspect media metadata
labs.task: Run exiftool and C2PA verification on sample files and judge authenticity from the output.

labs.title: Hunt automated login abuse
labs.task: Query authentication logs for high-speed credential attempts and write a rate-based detection.

checkpoint.focus: Deepfakes, voice cloning, AI phishing traits, automated attacks and verification controls

can_do: Perform a structured security review of an LLM application
Prioritize findings and map them to standard frameworks
Present remediation guidance to stakeholders

lessons.title: Scope and threat model the target app
lessons.goal: Document architecture, data flows, models and tools of the fictional app and identify the top threats.

lessons.title: Test and evidence the findings
lessons.goal: Probe for injection, leakage, excessive agency and supply chain flaws and collect reproducible evidence.

lessons.title: Report, prioritize and remediate
lessons.goal: Map findings to OWASP LLM and NIST AI RMF, rate severity and write a prioritized fix plan.

labs.title: Threat model the target app
labs.task: Diagram the app's components and annotate five prioritized AI-specific threats.

labs.title: Assess and report the app
labs.task: Review config, logs and chat transcripts, record findings with evidence and rank them by severity.

checkpoint.focus: End-to-end AI app review: threat model, evidence quality, severity ranking and remediation plan
